Kyoso no oni are the consummate assassins of the Shadowlands, infiltrating mortal society and eliminating dangers to the oni with an array of spell-like abilities. Fiercely cunning, the kyoso no oni are adept at blending into human society, often using seduction and trickery to gain close access to their targets before isolating and murdering them. Potential prey that proves resistant to these methods is not abandoned, however; the kyoso no oni merely assumes normal form in secret and stalks its victim underground.

A kyoso no oni attacks its prey from ambush, hoping to eliminate it quickly with its spell-like abilities and unholy fire. They only fight with their claws as a last resort. If overpowered, they will gladly flee in order to plan another strike.

Covert agents of the oni, shikibu no oni are commonly found in cities, working to bring the citizens to ruin. Cruel and mischievous, they delight in spreading lies, bringing disgrace to noble houses, and driving people into madness, Taint and ruin.

Shikibu no oni are almost never seen in their horrible natural forms, preferring to masquerade as one of the mortal races. Although they will adopt any form that suits their purposes, their favorite disguise is as a recently deceased resident of the community they are haunting, using this form to sow confusion and even working their way into a household to destroy it from within. Even when disguised, a shikibu no oni will maintain a lair in a nearby graveyard, where it will store its undead minions and have a constant supply of rotting corpses to feed on.

Shikibu no oni prefer to avoid combat whenever possible, changing their forms frequently and moving from place to place to avoid arousing suspicion. If forced into combat, they use their spell-like abilities to disable and hinder opponents while their undead minions do most of the dirty work.

The yattoko no oni are a reclusive breed of oni that bury themselves in the sands of Shadowlands deserts waiting for prey. Fairly intelligent, they still prefer the simple lifestyle of an animal, emerging from the sands only to feed. Yattoko no oni are among the most primitive of the oni, and they were among the first oni to be formed. As such, their memory stretches back much farther than those of most of their kind, and a yattoko no oni can be a valuable repository for planar lore. The problem lies, of course, in getting the oni to share its knowledge instead of just eating the supplicant.

Yattoko no oni are ambush hunters, bursting from the sands and grabbing a lone traveler, then disappearing again to finish its meal. If one finds itself in a fight with multiple opponents, it distracts opponents with summoned swarms and darkness before closing in on a weak-looking opponent to consume. Against heavily-armed warriors, they rely on their sundering rend.

sections.heading: Darkweaver
sections.text:
Few ever actually spy the darkweaver, shrouded in shadow as it most often keeps itself. When actually observed in the light, it at first glance resembles a massive spider, its skin oily and rubbery. The more one looks upon it, though, the more one sees how wrong this description is; rather than legs, each of its limbs is a long, writhing tentacle, wiry and quick. In place of mandibles, it bears short proboscises, thick probes that surround a mouth lined with razor-sharp fangs. Its body consists of two spherical segments, an abdomen and a head, and the only sensory organs a person can see are the dozens of pitch-dark orbs that dot its front without rhyme or reason, glimmering in the light before it extinguishes it once more.

html:
Darkweaver

Few ever actually spy the darkweaver, shrouded in shadow as it most often keeps itself. When actually observed in the light, it at first glance resembles a massive spider, its skin oily and rubbery. The more one looks upon it, though, the more one sees how wrong this description is; rather than legs, each of its limbs is a long, writhing tentacle, wiry and quick. In place of mandibles, it bears short proboscises, thick probes that surround a mouth lined with razor-sharp fangs. Its body consists of two spherical segments, an abdomen and a head, and the only sensory organs a person can see are the dozens of pitch-dark orbs that dot its front without rhyme or reason, glimmering in the light before it extinguishes it once more.

sections.heading: Ecalypse
sections.text:
Ecalypses are equine creatures that gallop across the Plane of Shadow in great herds. They’re often used as steeds by those powerful enough to tame them. Only at a great distance could an ecalypse be mistaken for a normal horse. The most obvious difference is its six legs, but other differences emerge on closer examination. Its coat is a flat gray that seems almost insubstantial—darker shadows beneath the skin reveal a rib cage, skull, and bones. The hooves fade off into tendrils of mist, as do the mane and tail. sections.heading: Umbral Banyan
sections.text:
Umbral banyans are the dark trees at the heart of many a dangerous forest. They blend in with other trees, strangling intruders with shadowy nooses that drop from the forest canopy. Though it lies perpetually in shadow, an umbral banyan otherwise looks just like the surrounding trees, only larger. Its massive root-and-trunk system can cover a thousand square feet or more, and its branches form an almost impenetrable ceiling 20 feet above the forest floor. Concealed among the branches are tendrils of inky blackness that slither around unwary victims, pulling them away from the ground and constricting them. Once the umbral banyan has strangled a victim, the tendrils toss the body among the exposed roots, where it decays and provides fertilizer for the tree.

sections.heading: GLOOM
sections.text:
The Gloom (it is hoped that there is only one) is an assassin of legendary repute from the Plane of Shadow. It is famous for the ability to kill―several victims at a time―and then depart again before guards and onlookers can even begin to react. in the warped reflection of the abandoned that cloaks itself in supernatural camouflage, lingering in the periphery of vision and stalking its prey from the deepest shadows. The Gloom looks very much like a human from the neck down, with dull, rubbery black skin. Its head, however, is another matter. Completely devoid of hair, the Gloom also has no eyes. Its distended, exaggerated mouth, drawn back in a perpetual fiendish smile, is full of jagged black teeth. Despite its apparent lack of ocular organs, the Gloom seems to have no trouble seeing. The Gloom typically dresses in fine clothing suitable for a funeral (stylized for the local culture), snug-fitting and all black.

sections.text:
Gloomwings are strange, moth-like natives of the Plane of Shadow. Despite their appearance, they are not vermin and possess a crude intelligence. sections.heading: Tenebrous Worm
sections.text:
For all the dangers a gloomwing presents, the creature’s young that pose a graver threat. The fact that a gloomwing can lay several eggs a day if presented with enough living hosts makes them dangerous not for what they can inflict themselves, but for what they can spawn.
The caterpillar-like tenebrous worm is a voracious predator that hungers for mortal flesh. The tenebrous worm is the larval stage of the gloomwing—but in a strange reversal, these younger creatures are more dangerous than the adults they grow into. A native of the Plane of Shadow, a tenebrous worm hatches from the body of an unfortunate creature that has been implanted with an egg by a gloomwing. The tenebrous worm is fully grown upon hatching, and immediately begins to scour its environs for flesh to consume.

Bristles (Su) Long bristles of shadowstuff extend from between the tenebrous worm’s armor plates. Those striking the worm with non-reach weapons take 1d6 piercing plus poison (DC 17 Reflex negates).
Although the tenebrous worm tends to be relatively pale-colored, its internal organs seethe and roil with shadowy energies and dark fluids. As the creature feeds, these shadowy innards begin to grow out of its body, forming strange bristle-like filaments of semisolid shadowstuff not only capable of piercing the flesh of those who would attack the worm, but also possessing a deadly paralytic poison. Additional shadowy fluids constantly seep from the worm’s mandibles—when it bites prey, these fluids melt flesh into shadows that the creature can then consume.
When a tenebrous worm feeds on enough of this shadowy flesh, the creature seeks out a secluded, shady area (typically just within a cave entrance or in a ruined building) and spins a shadowy cocoon around itself. After a period of several days, the cocoon tears open and a fully grown gloomwing emerges, ready to seek a host for its eggs.

An owb is a sinister visitor from the Shadow Plane, a creature resembling a humanoid torso draped in darkness. Alien in nature, this mysterious shade never speaks audible words, but it constantly uses its telepathy to project mumbles of curses and threats into the minds of those it encounters. The race’s closest relationship is with the dark folk, who worship owbs as proxies to gods of the shadows. Most dark folk believe the first of their kind were created by owbs—or more powerful owb-like beings.
An owb despises any light other than the dim flicker created by its burning cold ability, and shrinks from its presence. It often seeks to destroy those who bring light near it, relentlessly attacking the perpetrators until its enemies flee or die.
An owb usually keeps its presence hidden from mortals. Lurking nearby, the shadowy creature listens in on nearby thoughts, always searching for a collection of fears and worries it can capitalize on for its own machinations. It may serve as an intermediary between doppelgangers on the surface world and dark folk in subterranean lands. An owb associated with a tribe of dark folk may scrutinize newborns and tune the children’s connection to the Shadow Plane so they eventually grow into a different type of dark folk than the type they were born (allowing a dark creeper to become a dark stalker, and so on).
An owb loves manipulation and runs conspiratorial plots involving denizens of the Shadow Plane and those of the Material Plane. An owb or cabal of owbs may control entire clans of dark folk, and use them as spies and pawns in some inscrutable plan.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+3 Str, +4 Dex, +2 Con, -2 Int, +0 Wis, +2 Cha); racial feats: flight, telepathy; racial traits: fast (x2); aberrant gifts: fast healing, spell-like abilities.

sections.heading: SHADOW BEAST
sections.text:
Though they are called fiends and are usually evil, shadow beasts actually hail from the Plane of Shadow, not the Lower Planes whence come most fiends. There they serve powerful warlords— cloakers, nightshades, dread wraiths, and humanoids who have made their homes on that plane of darkness. They are equally happy to come to the Material Plane as mercenaries or regular soldiers in the hire of an evil lord.
On their native plane, the three varieties of shadow beast do not war against one another, but neither will they serve in the same company of soldiers. They do sometimes work together when serving on the Material Plane; in particular, the khumats seem able to cooperate with either of the other two varieties.

SHADOW BEAST

Though they are called fiends and are usually evil, shadow beasts actually hail from the Plane of Shadow, not the Lower Planes whence come most fiends. There they serve powerful warlords— cloakers, nightshades, dread wraiths, and humanoids who have made their homes on that plane of darkness. They are equally happy to come to the Material Plane as mercenaries or regular soldiers in the hire of an evil lord.

On their native plane, the three varieties of shadow beast do not war against one another, but neither will they serve in the same company of soldiers. They do sometimes work together when serving on the Material Plane; in particular, the khumats seem able to cooperate with either of the other two varieties.

This creature appears at first glance like a tiger or large panther with six limbs. Its face combines humanoid features with those of a big cat, and its expression is unmistakably malevolent. sections.heading: Shadowgarm
sections.text:
This amorphous creature loosely resembles a cross between a large snake and an insect. It has black oily skin, and parts of its very flesh blend seamlessly into the shadows. Its constantly moving, writhing form makes it difficult to identify from a distance. The typical shadowgarm measures about 4½ feet long and weighs approximately 90 pounds, their bodies being strangely light, composed of a spongy dark matter and seemingly wisps of shadow itself. Some, however, grow to be much larger, though shadowgarms of all sizes prove especially adept at blending in among the shadows and detritus of their hunting grounds or crawling into crevices it seems creatures of their size would not be able to squeeze.

Shadowgarms are strange monsters from the Plane of Shadow, where they function as lowly predators and pests somewhat akin to the Material Plane’s coyotes, leopards, and similar hunting mammals. Yet to a creature unfamiliar with the workings of the Plane of Shadow, the shadowgarm is a hideous and frightening beast. Generally lairing in ruined sections of towns or dead-end alleys clogged with refuse during the day, they come out at night to prey upon creatures that stray too far from the safety of light. These aberrant predators “leak” into the Material Plane anywhere the Plane of Shadow’s influence is strong. Small groups of shadowgarms are occasionally seen lurking in old graveyards where undead (particularly shadows) are known to reside, and anywhere that has strong traditions of shadow magic tends to have a healthy population of shadowgarms lurking in out-of-the-way areas as well.

sections.heading: Outsider
sections.text:
An outsider is at least partially composed of the essence (but not necessarily the material) of some plane other than the Material Plane. Some creatures start out as some other type and become outsiders when they attain a higher (or lower) state of spiritual existence. An outsider has the following features.
Physical Description: Almost any.
Type: Outsider. There are two primary subtypes: [extraplanar] and [native]; the former is assumed if the latter is not indicated. Outsiders from the Outer Planes (Heaven, the Abyss, etc.) also have the appropriate alignment descriptors; those from the Elemental Planes have those descriptors instead.
Languages: As appropriate to plane of origin—Abyssal, Aquan, Auran, Celestial, Ignan, Mabrahoring (AKA “Infernal”), Terran, etc.
Typical Classes: Any.
Attribute Modifiers: None unless granted by template.
Racial Feats: Outsiders have the following:
Darkvision 60 ft.Unlike most living creatures, an outsider does not have a dual nature—its soul and body form one unit. When an outsider is slain, no soul is set loose. Spells that restore souls to their bodies, such as raise dead, reincarnate, and resurrection, don't work on an outsider. It takes a different magical effect, such as limited wish, wish, miracle, or true resurrection to restore it to life.Any one feat for which the outsider meets the prerequisites. This can be traded for two racial traits (see Animals, et al.).
Racial Traits: Outsiders detect, and are affected by spells and abilities, as if they had the appropriate subtype and/or descriptors (see above). They do not need to eat or sleep (although they can do so if they wish).
Weapon Familiarity: Outsiders have one natural attack (typically claws or a bite). They can gain an additional natural attack as their racial feat. have no automatic weapon or armor proficiencies.
Special: A creature with outsider levels has the Outsider type, but can be based on a different creature type, using those racial characteristics instead of these.
Racial Progression: Outsiders progress using class levels or racial HD (see below). Levels in Outsider as treated as NPC class levels (2 per +1 to CR).

sections.heading: Abomination
sections.text:
Abominations are mistakes—the unwanted, unforeseen offspring of misguided deific concourse. Abortions of spirit, abominations live on, nurtured by their quasi-deific powers and pure, undiluted hate of their forebears and all naturally formed creatures.
Abominations are misshapen, grotesque, and horribly marked from their godly birth-throes. They come in an overwhelming variety of forms, all terrible. Accursed by heaven and hell, abominations are sealed away for aeons. But over the course of time, some are accidentally freed or manage to escape on their own. An abomination’s appearance can panic nations, worlds, or entire planes of existence. Thankfully, most abominations remain securely locked away by higher deific decree.
Abominations are built using a combination template that includes the Advanced simple template and the Half-Fiend template, the Monster of Legend templateMM2, and some additional immunities and special qualities. All abominations are of at least demigod status; some of them qualify as actual lesser gods (CR 21+).

sections.heading: Dream Larva
sections.text:
Most creatures know the startlement of a night terror—a bolt of horror that wakes the sleeper from a dead sleep. Dream larvae are night terrors that escape from dreams into the waking world, nightmares made manifest. Dream larvae are the misbegotten offspring of deities of fancy, longing, and dream. They have no specific form, but instead are every creature’s worst nightmare—each observer sees a dream larva for the first time as the most fearsome, terrible creature imaginable. To those that survive this initial vision, dream larvae appear as large humanoid shapes composed of thousands of crawling larval worms. Dream larvae have horns, cruelly fanged mouths, four arms ending in claws, and four other arms tipped with pincers.

sections.heading: Phaethon
sections.text:
“Nehwon’s blood,” Fafhrd was murmuring, his voice almost a chant, “still pulses strongly under its wrinkled rocky skin, and still bleeds hot and raw from wounds in the mountains… guard its mountain-wounds and wait and pray for the great day of fulfillment when Nehwon shall wake again, this time in man’s form, and rid itself of the vermin called men.”
―Fritz Leiber, “The Seven Black Priests” (1953)
Phaethons are the progeny of fire gods. No fire burns hotter than the rage personified by a phaethon. Gargantuan blots of sentient magma, phaethons burn their way through the belly of the earth. When roused, they burst to the surface, creating miniature volcanoes as they exit, and sweep upon the nearest flammable object or creature like a tsunami of red-hot liquid rock.

An uvuudaum is a manifestation of a distant realm where the rules of proper dimension are meaningless. When an uvuudaum manifests in common realms of matter and thought, it is terrible to behold.

Abomination

Abominations are mistakes—the unwanted, unforeseen offspring of misguided deific concourse. Abortions of spirit, abominations live on, nurtured by their quasi-deific powers and pure, undiluted hate of their forebears and all naturally formed creatures.

Abominations are misshapen, grotesque, and horribly marked from their godly birth-throes. They come in an overwhelming variety of forms, all terrible. Accursed by heaven and hell, abominations are sealed away for aeons. But over the course of time, some are accidentally freed or manage to escape on their own. An abomination’s appearance can panic nations, worlds, or entire planes of existence. Thankfully, most abominations remain securely locked away by higher deific decree.

Abominations are built using a combination template that includes the Advanced simple template and the Half-Fiend template, the Monster of Legend templateMM2, and some additional immunities and special qualities. All abominations are of at least demigod status; some of them qualify as actual lesser gods (CR 21+).

Phaethon

“Nehwon’s blood,” Fafhrd was murmuring, his voice almost a chant, “still pulses strongly under its wrinkled rocky skin, and still bleeds hot and raw from wounds in the mountains… guard its mountain-wounds and wait and pray for the great day of fulfillment when Nehwon shall wake again, this time in man’s form, and rid itself of the vermin called men.”

―Fritz Leiber, “The Seven Black Priests” (1953)

Phaethons are the progeny of fire gods. No fire burns hotter than the rage personified by a phaethon. Gargantuan blots of sentient magma, phaethons burn their way through the belly of the earth. When roused, they burst to the surface, creating miniature volcanoes as they exit, and sweep upon the nearest flammable object or creature like a tsunami of red-hot liquid rock.

Phanes are not so much captive as lost so far in the past (or future) that time itself is without meaning. However, sometimes a phane escapes into the four dimensions of our multiverse. Here, phanes particularly enjoy collecting victims by permanently locking them in temporal stasis. Phanes can feed off the essence of creatures they temporally trap in this fashion. Other phanes are more ambitious, and seek to alter the fate of nations, worlds, and planes—for the worse.

Phanes are most effective when they can get up close, drawing their potential victims into their null time field. If they can get hold of a target, they can temporally sequester their victim. If particularly threatened, a phane will use its time stop ability, use its chronal blast, then flee via teleport without error. The favorite tactic of a phane is to use its ability to summon a past time duplicate of a foe to sow confusion and uncertainty, prior to a full-out attack by the phane and a betrayal by the duplicate. An uvuudaum is a manifestation of a distant realm where the rules of proper dimension are meaningless. When an uvuudaum manifests in common realms of matter and thought, it is terrible to behold.

An uvuudaum appears as a vaguely humanoid creature with two standard human arms that protrude from the torso where expected, but whose lower body has six arms instead of legs, splayed spiderlike below it (tough loose clothing drapes its grotesque legs). The real horror is the tail-like appendage replacing what would be a head on a normal creature. At the very end of this appendage is an iron-hard spike.

More than one world’s arctic region provides a home for an unwanted child of chill deific lust. Frozen away for all time, xixecals could be released when some unrelated cataclysm causes the world to shudder and shake, cracking the xixecal free from its rigid prison of black ice. Thus, xixecals do not precipitate a time of change, but may accompany them.

Xixecals overcome most creatures merely by the shrieking supernatural storm of cold that accompanies them wherever they go. Those that can withstand the punishment of the storm are subject to a xixecal’s fearsome claws, bite, stamp, and rend—not to mention the white dragons that usually accompany a xixecal wherever it goes, glorying in the frigid calamity of its presence.

sections.heading: Akkorokamui
sections.text:
...three men, it was said, were out trying to catch a sword-fish, when all at once a great sea-monster, with large staring eyes, appeared in front of them and proceeded to attack the boat. The monster was round in shape, and emitted a dark fluid which has a very powerful and noxious odour.
―John Batchelor, The Ainu and Their Folk-Lore (1901)

The akkorokamui is a gigantic octopus-like monster from Ainu folklore, which supposedly lurks in Funka Bay in Hokkaidō and has been allegedly sighted in several locations including Taiwan and Korea since the 19th century. It is said that its enormous body can reach sizes of up to 120 meters in length. The coloration of the akkorokamui is said to be a striking red, often described as glowing and sometimes likened to the color of the reflection of the setting sun upon the water. Due to its coloration and immense size, it is visible from great distances.

CG Huge magical beast [aquatic]
Init +7; Senses low-light vision; Perception +8
Languages Celestial, Sylvan
AC 23, touch 11, flat-footed 21
(-2 size, +3 Dex, +12 natural)
hp 124 (12 HD; LW 62/HW 31); regeneration 5

1/day—restoration, atonement, heal
3/day—3rd--
At will—1st--, 2nd--

Skills Escape Artist +18, Perception +8, Stealth +18, Swim +13
Environment any ocean
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Ainu reverence of this monster has permeated into Shintoism, which has incorporated the akkorokamui as a minor kami. While Akkorokamui is often presented as a benevolent kami with powers to heal and bestow knowledge, it is fickle and has the propensity to do harm. Akkorokamui’s nature as an octopus means that it is persistent and it is near impossible to escape its grasp without permission. Like other Shinto purification rituals, prior to entering the shrine of Akkorokamui, one’s hands must be cleaned with water with the exception that one’s feet must also be cleaned as well. Akkorokamui enjoys the sea and offerings which reflect this: fish, crab, mollusks, and the like are particular favorites of Akkorokamui, which give back that which it gave. Homage to Akkorokamui is often for ailments of the limbs or skin, but mental purification and spiritual release is particularly important.

sections.heading: Ethergaunt
sections.text:
Travelers to the Ethereal Plane report vast fields of nothingness, roiling fog cloaking a barren landscape. Sometimes, however, they come upon fantastic stone pyramids or cyclopean menhirs topped with flashing magical flames, relics of an ancient race. Scholars refer to the fearsome creators of these structures as ethergaunts, after their emaciated, delicate frames. An advanced culture that abandoned the Material Plane more than 10,000 years ago, the ethergaunts are finally coming back.
Type: Aberration [extraplanar].
Languages: Khen-Zai; others.
Typical Classes: Wizard.
Attribute Modifiers: Str -2, Int +2, Cha +2.
Racial Feats: Blindsight (40 ft.), Favored Terrain (Ethereal Plane).
Racial Traits: Scaling favored terrain.
Weapon Familiarity: Exotic Weapon Proficiency (halberd). All ethergaunts are proficient with this so-called “etherblade.”

sections.heading: Red Ethergaunt
sections.text:
The most frequently encountered caste of ethergaunts, reds serve the race as scouts and low-level diplomats (particularly when diplomacy in fact means exterminating natives to send a political message). Though they hold an arrogant opinion of their own importance in relation to the current residents of the Material Plane, reds fully understand their role as the rank-and-file of the ether legions. The fact that ethergaunt grunts generally are more brilliant than the brightest human mages reveals much regarding their perspective.

sections.heading: White Ethergaunt
sections.text:
White ethergaunts, who serve the race as scholars, philosophers, diplomats, and bureaucrats, occasionally parley with the Material Plane races in order to serve the greater goal of planar domination. Cunning schemers, whites attempt to purge all emotion from their dealings, instead dedicating themselves to an objective (in their view) pragmatism. Whites seldom give an inch, and “negotiations” generally boil down to suggestions that fighting off inevitable genocide will only result in unnecessary struggle and needless destruction of material resources.

Ethergaunt

Travelers to the Ethereal Plane report vast fields of nothingness, roiling fog cloaking a barren landscape. Sometimes, however, they come upon fantastic stone pyramids or cyclopean menhirs topped with flashing magical flames, relics of an ancient race. Scholars refer to the fearsome creators of these structures as ethergaunts, after their emaciated, delicate frames. An advanced culture that abandoned the Material Plane more than 10,000 years ago, the ethergaunts are finally coming back.

Type: Aberration [extraplanar].

Languages: Khen-Zai; others.

Typical Classes: Wizard.

Attribute Modifiers: Str -2, Int +2, Cha +2.

Racial Feats: Blindsight (40 ft.), Favored Terrain (Ethereal Plane).

Racial Traits: Scaling favored terrain.

Weapon Familiarity: Exotic Weapon Proficiency (halberd). All ethergaunts are proficient with this so-called “etherblade.”

Red Ethergaunt

The most frequently encountered caste of ethergaunts, reds serve the race as scouts and low-level diplomats (particularly when diplomacy in fact means exterminating natives to send a political message). Though they hold an arrogant opinion of their own importance in relation to the current residents of the Material Plane, reds fully understand their role as the rank-and-file of the ether legions. The fact that ethergaunt grunts generally are more brilliant than the brightest human mages reveals much regarding their perspective.

White Ethergaunt

White ethergaunts, who serve the race as scholars, philosophers, diplomats, and bureaucrats, occasionally parley with the Material Plane races in order to serve the greater goal of planar domination. Cunning schemers, whites attempt to purge all emotion from their dealings, instead dedicating themselves to an objective (in their view) pragmatism. sections.heading: Gingwatzim
sections.text:
Gingwatzim are beings or raw spirit energy from the Ethereal Plane, where they normally reside. There are six species of gingwatzim: the tim, pakim, graegzim, eoluzim, maronzim, and naranzim. In their free form, gingwatzim appear as glowing spheres with distinct colors. For example, the tim species is blue and the naranzim is a bright red-orange. In free form, gingwatzim float or flit around like fireflies.
Their statistics are derived using the Gingwatzim templates described below, and by adding Outsider racial HD.
Gingwatzim	Cr +1
Type outsider [incorporeal]
Size as with ghosts, when gaining the Giant or Young simple template, incorporeal creatures do not gain bonuses to Str or natural armor, and also do not take Dex penalties. Instead, apply the +4 Str bonus to Cha.
AC deflection bonus equal to Charisma bonus
Spd fly 40 ft.
Melee gingwatzim have an incorporeal touch attack that deals Strength damage scaling with the creature’s size (base 1d4 for Medium). Creatures damaged to 0 Str or below by this attack become comatose, and cannot move.
Attributes +2 Wisdom
SQ Bound Form (Su): Once a gingwatzim has been bound to service, it may also be given either an animate or inanimate form. These are the three typical states in which a gingwatzim may be encountered. After conjured to this plane and bound in one of the forms, a gingwatzim may not return to its own plane unless it is freed by the conjurer; it is slain in free or animate form; it is destroyed while in inanimate form; or its conjurer or current owner dies. Once the conjurer has chosen the forms, they are invariable. Control of the gingwatzim can be transferred along with possession of the spirit when it is in its inanimate form, if the conjurer so wishes (the gingwatzim still counts against the conjurer’s thaumaturgy limit.
A gingwatzim’s animate form is a creature of the same CR or less; it functions as if by a possession spell, but of unlimited duration. Its inanimate form can be any item worth less than or equal to the gingwatzim’s NPC numen limit. Note that the gingwatzim itself pays this cost while in that form, not the conjurer. The item and/or animate body must be present when the gingwatzim is summoned.

Melee increase Str damage by 1 die step
Spell-Like Abilities gain racial suite as shown

html:
Gingwatzim

Gingwatzim are beings or raw spirit energy from the Ethereal Plane, where they normally reside. There are six species of gingwatzim: the tim, pakim, graegzim, eoluzim, maronzim, and naranzim. In their free form, gingwatzim appear as glowing spheres with distinct colors. For example, the tim species is blue and the naranzim is a bright red-orange. In free form, gingwatzim float or flit around like fireflies.

Their statistics are derived using the Gingwatzim templates described below, and by adding Outsider racial HD.

Gingwatzim Cr +1

Type outsider [incorporeal]

Size as with ghosts, when gaining the Giant or Young simple template, incorporeal creatures do not gain bonuses to Str or natural armor, and also do not take Dex penalties. Instead, apply the +4 Str bonus to Cha.

AC deflection bonus equal to Charisma bonus

Spd fly 40 ft.

Melee gingwatzim have an incorporeal touch attack that deals Strength damage scaling with the creature’s size (base 1d4 for Medium). Creatures damaged to 0 Str or below by this attack become comatose, and cannot move.

Attributes +2 Wisdom

SQ Bound Form (Su): Once a gingwatzim has been bound to service, it may also be given either an animate or inanimate form. These are the three typical states in which a gingwatzim may be encountered. After conjured to this plane and bound in one of the forms, a gingwatzim may not return to its own plane unless it is freed by the conjurer; it is slain in free or animate form; it is destroyed while in inanimate form; or its conjurer or current owner dies. Once the conjurer has chosen the forms, they are invariable. Control of the gingwatzim can be transferred along with possession of the spirit when it is in its inanimate form, if the conjurer so wishes (the gingwatzim still counts against the conjurer’s thaumaturgy limit.

A gingwatzim’s animate form is a creature of the same CR or less; it functions as if by a possession spell, but of unlimited duration. Its inanimate form can be any item worth less than or equal to the gingwatzim’s NPC numen limit. Note that the gingwatzim itself pays this cost while in that form, not the conjurer. The item and/or animate body must be present when the gingwatzim is summoned.

HD increase by 1

Resist SR equal to CR + 14 + Cha modifier

Melee increase Str damage by 1 die step

Spell-Like Abilities gain racial suite as shown

Attributes +2 to all

sections.heading: Gorgon, High
sections.text:
A high gorgon resembles a solidly-built human with slightly grayish, almost glistening skin. They have no body hair whatsoever—a fact that they often conceal with cosmetics, hoods or wigs. A small seam runs from the bottom of the breastbone down to just above the genitals. When the high gorgon wishes to reveal its true nature, the seam splits wide open, revealing a mass of intertwined serpents that strike out at the gorgon's enemies. High gorgons usually have yellow, amber or brown eyes, and their teeth are unusually perfect.

One of the most twisted legacies that the Titans left behind is Mormo's parting gift to the world — the gorgons. These wretched creatures were birthed by the Serpentmother some 50 years before the Titanswar, and they served their mother obediently. They were certainly her most faithful creation. Now that Mormo has been hacked apart and buried, the gorgons work secretly to restore her.
There are two varieties of gorgon—the bestial low gorgon, and the humanoid high gorgon. Although nearly as different as humans and lions, both varieties of gorgon are repulsively interfertile; the females of both species can be fertilized by males of either kind. They lay clutches of 1d6 eggs, one in five of which typically hatches into a high gorgon—the rest become low gorgons.

sections.text:
A low gorgon looks something like a reptilian lion, with a ruff of writhing snaky tendrils where a mane would be. Its dark-green scales are thick, almost metallic, and its long, flexible tail ends in a bony knob like a mace.

2 claws +12 (1d6+7) and tail slap +12 (1d6+7)

Attributes Str 24, Dex 15, Con 22, Int 7, Wis 16,  Cha 12
Feats Dodge, Improved Multiattack, Skirmish, Toughness, Weapon Specialization (bite)
Skills Athletics (5/+15), Perception (9/+15), Stealth (9/+10), Survival (4/+10)
Environment temperate and warm forests, hills, and underground
Frequency uncommon
Organization pack (2-5) or herd (6-30)
Treasure standard
It seems impossible to believe that the bestial low gorgons are related to their humanoid cousins, but that's exactly the case. Where the high gorgons are intelligent and subtle, the low gorgons are ravening and animalistic. Still, the blood of Mormo ties them to their bipedal cousins, and the two races are often found in one another's company.

A low gorgon typically focuses its claws and bite on one opponent, not relenting until it has felt its victim die in its jaws; it reserves its tail lash attack for those trying to flank it. When they hunt in packs, low gorgons demonstrate even further cunning, seeking out spellcasters, archers and other ranged combatants actively. (They even leap over the heads of defenders if necessary.) If directed by a high gorgon, low gorgons are capable of following complicated plans, although their natural impatience can sometimes hinder their efficiency.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: standard; racial feats: additional traits, intractable, multiattack; racial traits: fast (x2), open minded (x2); special attacks: acid bite, additional natural attack (tail).

sections.heading: Impundulu

The Xosas call this bird impundulu—a name nowadays adopted for an electric tram-car! It is said to “appear as such”—that is to say, in its proper form, as a bird... when it darts down as lightning, people only see the flash.
―Alice Werner, Myths and Legends of the Bantu (1968)

A dark shadow moves rapidly across the ground. In the skies high above, silhouetted by the sun, a monstrous, black-feathered avian creature circles. Slowly, a supernatural wind begins to swirl about the creature, and crackling sparks erupt from its body. Screeching wildly, it descends as if falling from the sky, its blood-flecked wings tipped with cruel curved hooks, and its protruding lower beak scalloped with vicious, jagged barbs.

The tribesfolk of southern Garund tell tales of a ruthless winged shapeshifter, a bloodthirsty demon and hunter of men. They call this being impundulu, a name that loosely translates to “lightning-bird” after its savage avian form. Legend describes this creature as a huge, stork-like bird that rides upon fierce storms and whose dark feathers crackle with lightning. It is believed that an evil shaman summoned the first impundulu and that using an ancient, taboo ritual, the two formed a blood pact. The shaman offered the impundulu the ability to wear his mortal flesh in exchange for mastery over the demon’s significant occult powers. As soon as the impundulu seized control of the shaman’s body, it broke the pact; however, the ancient ritual bound the fiend to the mortal form, and even after the shaman perished, it could not shed its flesh. Thus, despite its own immortality, the impundulu became forever tied to the realm of mortals. For this reason, it is said, the creature continues to forge pacts with mortal spellcasters in the hope that one day it will unbind the secrets of its cursed existence.
Most of the time, the fiend hunts in its avian form. A hideous thing of similar appearance to a large stork or vulture, it’s readily identified by its distinctive long, jagged beak and its slender wings that each bear a hidden, hooked claw. Despite the creature’s intelligence, it behaves barbarically and delights in gory slaughter. It precedes physical attacks by conjuring fierce, wrathful blasts of lightning to confuse and injure prey, then swoops in to rend its prey to pieces.
In its humanoid form, the impundulu manifests as a strikingly handsome man with glistening, coal-black skin, whose eyes burn a pale, otherworldly green. His legs end in monstrous raptor’s talons, and his black fingernails hang long and curved. Using this form, an impundulu can wander through villages, stalking and seducing women with lies and magic, and preying upon them by draining their blood. The creature rarely uses its humanoid form, reserving it for times it wishes to engage in subtle cruelties.

The Xosas call this bird impundulu—a name nowadays adopted for an electric tram-car! It is said to “appear as such”—that is to say, in its proper form, as a bird... when it darts down as lightning, people only see the flash.

sections.heading: Keeper
sections.text:
A keeper looks human at first glance, but a close examination reveals that its bald, pale -skinned, humanoid form moves oddly; all its joints are capable of bending in any direction. Adding to their alien appearance, keepers all look remarkably similar; each wears a dark leather coat that serves as armor and black goggles to disguise the fact that the creatures have no eyes.

Environment any (unknown plane)
Frequency very rare

Treasure half standard

Dissolution (Sp) Damage attribute (Con; 1st level) + Extend Spell (inst. to 1 rd./level; +2 levels) + Tenuous Spell (-1 level) + Shape Spell (target to spread; +2 levels) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 5’r.; ­2 levels) + Delay Spell (see below; +1 level) = 3rd level; a keeper that is killed or restrained for more than 10 rounds dissolves into a 5’r. pool of poison (1d4 Con/rd. for 8 rds. or until save).
Mimic Weapons (Ex) A keeper can mold one or both hands into any normal melee weapon (mimicking a two-handed weapon requires both hands).
Some sages believe that keepers were someone’s attempt to create a race of constructs that would act as spies or guardians of some secret knowledge. At some point the process went awry, and keepers began to be born as free-willed living beings. Now they roam the planes, driven to discover the secrets of others and make certain that no one else can learn them. Others maintain that keepers were instead found, and are only tentatively controlled.
Keepers are driven to discover things that others do not want known. They are insatiably curious, but prefer to observe the knowledge they seek rather than interact with the creatures that have it. Once they have learned what they think they can from a creature, keepers often attempt to silence that creature so that others cannot learn what it knows. Despite these draconian tactics, keepers can be bargained with and will hold to the letter of any deal made. Such bargains usually involve simply buying off the keepers with knowledge rather than an exchange of information: No keeper willingly parts with its secrets.
Keepers have a disturbing and abrupt manner, finding the subtleties of the cultures of other creatures chaotic and difficult to understand. Keepers seem too intense and driven to most creatures and are often unsettling to others even when they are trying to be diplomatic.
The keepers’ mental organization seems to preclude individuality in the sense that most mortals possess. Keepers have no names, but are called “First,” “Second,” etc. Each group of keepers has a group identity that follows the numeric designation: the Apotheosis, the Colorless Pool, the Darkened Sun, the Draeden, the Iron Flask, the Maze, the Mists, the Gray Path, the Seven Parts, the Ur-Fiend, and the Unliving God are some noted ones.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+4 Str, +3 Dex, +2 Con, +2 Int, -2 Wis, +0 Cha); racial feats: blindsense, scent; racial traits: ferocity, improve blindsense to blindsight; aberrant gifts: immunity, mimic weapons, poison, spell-like abilities. Note that this keeper has most of the abilities listed in the source material and the same CR, but is a far more effective melee combatant.

sections.heading: Negative Energy Plane
sections.text: Although in 3.0/3.5 edition D&D these creatures are specifically considered outsiders, rather than undead, the distinction is blurry because undead are specifically healed by negative energy. Combines with the fact that these beings are incorporeal (prompting the use of the Ghost template, q.v.), treating them as extraplanar undead seemed the simplest approach in terms of converting them using these rules.

sections.heading: Drelb
sections.text:
Drelbs are energy creatures that make their home on the Negative Energy Plane. They are summoned to the Material Plane by evil spellcasters who task them with the duty of guarding treasure or secret places to be left alone. Hence, they are sometimes referred to as “haunting custodians.” A drelb resembles and is nearly indistinguishable from a wraith; a DC 20 Knowledge (the planes) check will reveal that it is actually a native of the Negative Energy Plane with undead-like traits, and a DC 25 check identifies the creature for what it is.

Incorporeal creatures, xag-yas and xeg-yis take no notice of features such as doors, walls, and furniture, silently gliding from place to place on unknowable errands. They often pause to observe other creatures, tending to favor places where birth or death is occurring. Energons rarely start fights, but their mere touch is dangerous, so many creatures consider them a threat and try to drive them off.

Negative Energy Plane

Although in 3.0/3.5 edition D&D these creatures are specifically considered outsiders, rather than undead, the distinction is blurry because undead are specifically healed by negative energy. Combines with the fact that these beings are incorporeal (prompting the use of the Ghost template, q.v.), treating them as extraplanar undead seemed the simplest approach in terms of converting them using these rules.

Drelb

Drelbs are energy creatures that make their home on the Negative Energy Plane. They are summoned to the Material Plane by evil spellcasters who task them with the duty of guarding treasure or secret places to be left alone. Hence, they are sometimes referred to as “haunting custodians.” A drelb resembles and is nearly indistinguishable from a wraith; a DC 20 Knowledge (the planes) check will reveal that it is actually a native of the Negative Energy Plane with undead-like traits, and a DC 25 check identifies the creature for what it is.

sections.heading: Shroudling
sections.text:
"We are among the last of the shroudlings. There are only five families of us left in all the secret images of all the shadows from here to Amber—and farther, on into that place and into Chaos."
I held her more tightly and a long lifetime of strange lore passed through my head. Later I said, "Sorry, but I have no idea of what a shroudling is."
Later still she responded, "I would be very surprised if you did, for we have always been a secret race."
"You came in by way of the mirror?"
"I did. I live in the mirrorworld."
"And your family? And the four other families you mentioned?"
"We all of us make our homes beyond the bounds of reflection."
"And from there you travel from place to place?"
"Indeed."
―Roger Zelazny,
“The Shroudling and the Guisel” (1994)
Some scholars maintain that the common belief that mirrors simply reflect light is wrong—in truth, they allow the viewer to gaze into a reality that exists alongside the one they know. That reality is known as the Plane of Mirrors. The inhabitants of the Plane of Mirrors are the creatures known as shroudlings, of which only five families exist; two of those families, the Nerra and the Soulslivers, are detailed here.
Shroudlings are built using a simple variant on the half-celestial templatePB:
Shroudling	Cr +2
Type changes to outsider [mirror]
Senses mirror sight (Su) while on the Plane of Mirrors, a shroudling can see into the Material Plane through any mundane mirror or other reflective surface there, as if it were a window.
AC +1 to natural armor; DR 5/bludgeoning
Immune gaze attacks
Resist cold 10, electricity 10, fire 10; SR 14 + CR + Cha modifier.
Reflective Spell Resistance (Su) any spell individually targeting the shroudling that is successfully resisted reflects back at the caster, who becomes the spell’s target.
Weaknesses vulnerability to sonic
Spd mirror jump (Su) In lieu of a fly speed, a shroudling gains the ability to travel through mirrors at will. This effect is similar to tree stride or shadow walk, but the shroudling travels along the Plane of Mirrors. As a standard action, the shroudling must touch a mirror or other highly reflective surface. He or she then exits from another mirror that is no farther than 1 mile away. If the shroudling touches a regular mirror, the mirror jump happens automatically. A shroudling can also touch a highly reflective surface, such as a polished metal shield or armor. This surface must be clear glass, a still pool of water, or shiny metal. There is a 50% chance that the surface is reflective enough to make the mirror jump. However, a shroudling can only enter a non-mirrored surface—it can return only through a normal mirror. If another mirror is not within the range of the mirror jump, the shroudling must wander the Plane of Mirrors and exit through another random mirror portal.
Spell-Like Abilities (Sp) A Nerra’s suite of racial spell-like abilities is as follows: 1st—disguise self, 2nd—mirror image, 3rd—shard spray (see below), 4th—false vision, 5th—plane shift (Prime Material/Plane of Mirrors only, through a mirror), 6th—mislead, 7th—spell turning, 8th—maze, 9th—affinity fieldSRD. It is assumed that the other shroudling families’ abilities are similar, but this has not been ascertained.
Attributes +4 to any 3 attributes; +2 to the remaining three

sections.heading: Nerra
sections.text:
Enigmatic and contrary by nature, Nerras lurk the eternal hallways of the Plane of Mirrors, observing activities on the Material Plane by looking through any of the countless mirrors that serve as conduits between the two planes.
Nerras look like normal humanoids, but they have skin with a perfectly mirror-like smooth surface. Nerras occasionally cross the border between the planes to kidnap individuals on the Material Plane. It has been theorized that they are planning an invasion of the Material Plane. Sometimes Nerras wander the Planes, gathering information and infiltrating a variety of organizations. Some monitor the activity of a wide range of people; others have a particular “pet,” or favorite. These are usually, but not always, individuals in positions of power. After a while, the nerra may try to capture the individual and bring him or her onto the Plane of Mirrors.
Nerras are accomplished and sneaky fighters that use ambush and cover to bring down their opponents. They prefer to lurk on the Plane of Mirrors and surprise an opponent by leaping out of a mirror. If a Nerra is planning on kidnapping a victim, it uses weapons and techniques that capture or cause subdual damage. When killed, a Nerra shatters into a thousand mirror-like shards. After about 10 minutes, these shards turn into pools of quicksilver before fading away into nothing.

While Nerras are usually stealthy in combat, there are times when brute force is necessary. This special breed of warriors is called the kalareems, and they are ferocious warriors that fight with two shard swords. They are the chosen defenders of the Plane of Mirrors. Kalareems are bulky and muscular; instead of the smooth, naked form of varoots, they wear mirrored armor that seems to blend in with their natural form. They are quiet and taciturn, and they fight with fluid grace.
Kalareems move and fight with deadly accuracy, and they seem to flow more than walk. Kalareems prefer to soften up a target from a distance with their shard spray and will usually exhaust this option before moving into melee.

Unlike varoots or kalareems, sillits prefer to wear clothing such as fine silk robes of shiny black with large hoods.

sections.heading: Soulsliver
sections.text:
This smooth-featured, humanoid creature appears to have skin made entirely of mirrored glass. A soulsliver is an extradimensional shapechanger that lurks in the half-dimensions behind mirrors. It watches creatures on the Material Plane through reflective surfaces, assumes their likeness, then crawls through the mirror to kill and feast upon its prey. Whether they are bizarre offshoots of the doppelganger race or originate from some aberrant magic used to create a demiplane, soulslivers are responsible for many unsolved murders, and their mirror travel makes them hard to catch.

Shroudling

"We are among the last of the shroudlings. There are only five families of us left in all the secret images of all the shadows from here to Amber—and farther, on into that place and into Chaos."

I held her more tightly and a long lifetime of strange lore passed through my head. Later I said, "Sorry, but I have no idea of what a shroudling is."

Later still she responded, "I would be very surprised if you did, for we have always been a secret race."

"You came in by way of the mirror?"

"I did. I live in the mirrorworld."

"And your family? And the four other families you mentioned?"

"We all of us make our homes beyond the bounds of reflection."

"And from there you travel from place to place?"

"Indeed."

―Roger Zelazny,

“The Shroudling and the Guisel” (1994)

Some scholars maintain that the common belief that mirrors simply reflect light is wrong—in truth, they allow the viewer to gaze into a reality that exists alongside the one they know. That reality is known as the Plane of Mirrors. The inhabitants of the Plane of Mirrors are the creatures known as shroudlings, of which only five families exist; two of those families, the Nerra and the Soulslivers, are detailed here.

Shroudlings are built using a simple variant on the half-celestial templatePB:

Shroudling Cr +2

Type changes to outsider [mirror]

Senses mirror sight (Su) while on the Plane of Mirrors, a shroudling can see into the Material Plane through any mundane mirror or other reflective surface there, as if it were a window.

AC +1 to natural armor; DR 5/bludgeoning

Immune gaze attacks

Resist cold 10, electricity 10, fire 10; SR 14 + CR + Cha modifier.

Reflective Spell Resistance (Su) any spell individually targeting the shroudling that is successfully resisted reflects back at the caster, who becomes the spell’s target.

Weaknesses vulnerability to sonic

Spd mirror jump (Su) In lieu of a fly speed, a shroudling gains the ability to travel through mirrors at will. This effect is similar to tree stride or shadow walk, but the shroudling travels along the Plane of Mirrors. As a standard action, the shroudling must touch a mirror or other highly reflective surface. He or she then exits from another mirror that is no farther than 1 mile away. If the shroudling touches a regular mirror, the mirror jump happens automatically. A shroudling can also touch a highly reflective surface, such as a polished metal shield or armor. This surface must be clear glass, a still pool of water, or shiny metal. There is a 50% chance that the surface is reflective enough to make the mirror jump. However, a shroudling can only enter a non-mirrored surface—it can return only through a normal mirror. If another mirror is not within the range of the mirror jump, the shroudling must wander the Plane of Mirrors and exit through another random mirror portal.

Spell-Like Abilities (Sp) A Nerra’s suite of racial spell-like abilities is as follows: 1st—disguise self, 2nd—mirror image, 3rd—shard spray (see below), 4th—false vision, 5th—plane shift (Prime Material/Plane of Mirrors only, through a mirror), 6th—mislead, 7th—spell turning, 8th—maze, 9th—affinity fieldSRD. It is assumed that the other shroudling families’ abilities are similar, but this has not been ascertained.

Attributes +4 to any 3 attributes; +2 to the remaining three

Nerra

Enigmatic and contrary by nature, Nerras lurk the eternal hallways of the Plane of Mirrors, observing activities on the Material Plane by looking through any of the countless mirrors that serve as conduits between the two planes.

Nerras look like normal humanoids, but they have skin with a perfectly mirror-like smooth surface. Nerras occasionally cross the border between the planes to kidnap individuals on the Material Plane. It has been theorized that they are planning an invasion of the Material Plane. Sometimes Nerras wander the Planes, gathering information and infiltrating a variety of organizations. Some monitor the activity of a wide range of people; others have a particular “pet,” or favorite. These are usually, but not always, individuals in positions of power. After a while, the nerra may try to capture the individual and bring him or her onto the Plane of Mirrors.

Nerras are accomplished and sneaky fighters that use ambush and cover to bring down their opponents. They prefer to lurk on the Plane of Mirrors and surprise an opponent by leaping out of a mirror. If a Nerra is planning on kidnapping a victim, it uses weapons and techniques that capture or cause subdual damage. When killed, a Nerra shatters into a thousand mirror-like shards. After about 10 minutes, these shards turn into pools of quicksilver before fading away into nothing.

While Nerras are usually stealthy in combat, there are times when brute force is necessary. This special breed of warriors is called the kalareems, and they are ferocious warriors that fight with two shard swords. They are the chosen defenders of the Plane of Mirrors. Kalareems are bulky and muscular; instead of the smooth, naked form of varoots, they wear mirrored armor that seems to blend in with their natural form. They are quiet and taciturn, and they fight with fluid grace.

Kalareems move and fight with deadly accuracy, and they seem to flow more than walk. Kalareems prefer to soften up a target from a distance with their shard spray and will usually exhaust this option before moving into melee.

Sillits are the leaders, planners, and schemers of the Nerras. Unless urgent business takes them to the Material Plane, sillits rarely leave the safety of the Plane of Mirrors. Physically, sillits look like other Nerras. They have a humanoid shape covered with mirror-like skin, and their faces are completely smooth. This smooth-featured, humanoid creature appears to have skin made entirely of mirrored glass. A soulsliver is an extradimensional shapechanger that lurks in the half-dimensions behind mirrors. sections.heading: Psychopomp
sections.text:
As the spirits of the deceased flow from the confusion of mortality to their ultimate fates, they are each judged by the gods of death, who assure that all who die reach their prescribed afterlife. Yet with all the worlds of the Material Plane, the countless faces and exceptions of mortality, death as a system and institution requires more agents than a single deity or pantheon to uphold. These agents are the psychopomps—denizens of Purgatory and the dispassionate stewards and guides of all that die.
As psychopomps help convey souls to all of the Outer Planes, and thus provide petitioners equally to each of those realms, they enjoy a special status among many planar races as respected neutrals. As such, most other planar races grant them a wide berth, with even archons and demons going out of their ways to avoid interfering with death’s emissaries. Soul-hungry daemons and reality-violating qlippoth are among the only races that actively oppose psychopomps. Consequently, the deadlier classes of psychopomps watch for and hunt disruptive members of these races, seeking to expunge the paths between the planes of any that would impede the certain cycle of death.
Psychopomps are constructed using a template, based on the half-celestial and half-fiend templates with modifications:
Psychopomp	Cr +2
Type outsider [extraplanar, psychopomp]
Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, spirit sense (Su): a psychopomp notices, locates, and can distinguish between living and undead creatures within 60 feet, just as if it had the blindsight ability. This sense does not allow it to detect objects.
Languages Abyssal, Celestial, Mabrahoring (Int allowing); tongues; telepathy
AC +2 to natural armor
DR 5/adamantine (10 if CR 6+)
Immune afflictions, [death] effects
Resist cold 10, electricity 10; SR 14 + CR + Cha modifier
Spd 30 ft., fly 50 ft. for winged psychopomps
Melee natural weapons (2 slams, or 2 claws, etc.; base damage 1d8 for Medium)
Spell-Like Abilities (Sp) psychopomps receive 2 suites of racial spell-like abilities.
Attributes +4 to any 3; +2 to remaining 3
Feats Ghost StrikeB, Permanent SpellB (aura—varies by psychopomp type)

sections.heading: Psychopomp, Catrina
sections.text:
With lengthy curling hair, a dancer’s dress, and a bouquet of flowers, this woman remains beautiful, despite having no flesh. Catrinas always appear as festively dressed skeletons—usually in women’s garb but sometimes in colorful men’s formal wear, and usually decorated with or carrying f lowers. They do not have true genders, but an individual catrina may have a more masculine or feminine voice and personality. They typically stand between 5 and 6 feet tall and weigh about 20 to 30 pounds.
CatrinaPB4	Cr 5
Half-advanced, psyhopomp outsider 6
LG Medium outsider [archon]
Init +7; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, planar sense 5 ft., spirit sense 60 ft.;
Perception +12
Aura calm emotions 10 ft.
Languages Celestial, Mabrahoring; tongues; telepathy 40 ft.
AC 19, touch 13, flat-footed 16 (+3 Dex, +6 natural)
hp 51 (6 HD; LW 25/HW 12); DR 5/adamantine
Immune afflictions, [death] effects
Resist cold 10, electricity 10; SR 24
Fort +5, Ref +7, Int +4, Will +11; resolve
Spd 30 ft.
Melee 2 slams +8 (1d8+2)
Base Atk +6; CMB +8; CMD 17
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 6th)
1/day—compel condemned (see below; DC 17), deathwatch, major image (DC 18), speak with dead
At will—dancing lights, charm person (DC 16), kiss of death (see below)
Attributes Str 14, Dex 17, Con 16, Int 13, Wis 14, Cha 20
Feats Improved Initiative, Ghost StrikeB, Iron Will, Killing Stroke, Permanent SpellB (aura)
Skills Bluff (6/+14), Concentration (6/+14), Diplomacy (6/+14), Knowledge (planes) (6/+10), Perception (6/+11), Planar Sense (6/+11), Stealth (6/+12)

Environment any (Purgatory)
Frequency common
Organization solitary, pair, or reception (3–10)
Treasure standard
Calm Emotions Aura (Sp) Warding (emotion and morale effects; 1st level) + Tenacious Spell (+1 level) + Shape Spell (target to emanation; +2 levels) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 10’r.; -1 level) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 1 hr./level; +2 levels) + Irresistible Spell (non-magic emotions also suppressed; +2 levels) + Pacific Spell (-2 levels) + Restricted Spell (psychopomp; -1 level) = 3rd level.
Compel Condemned (Sp) Compel (approach and kiss; 2nd level) + Extend Spell (1 rd. to 1 rd./level; +2 levels) + Pacific Spell (-2 levels) = 2nd level; as a standard action, a catrina can force one humanoid within Close range to approach and kiss her. This action is not considered to be against the target’s nature or self-destructive. Any damage taken by the target (other than damage the catrina deals) immediately ends this effect.
Kiss of Death (Sp) Ray of entropy (1st level) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) + Concentration Spell (standard; +2 levels) + Reduce Spell (10d6 to 5d6; -1 level) = 1st level; a catrina’s kiss deals 5d6 necrotic damage as a melee touch attack, and when continued counts as studying the victim for purposes of eventually using it to activate a Killing Stroke.
Catrinas welcome the dead into the afterlife, doing what they can to lessen the shock and terror experienced by mortals who haven’t accepted their own deaths or who still grieve for themselves. Eschewing the funereal themes and colors preferred by most other psychopomps, catrinas dress in festive shades, surrounding themselves with light and color to dispel a measure of death’s gloom. However, they don’t disguise their skeletal bodies, for despite any gilding they might put on the moment, they don’t seek to disguise the finality of death. A catrina’s motivation for easing the transition from life to death has more to do with making the soul’s progression calm than compassion for the soul—screaming and outrage disrupt the processing of the dead.
Catrinas rarely ever visit the Material Plane, but when they do so it’s typically at the command of a more powerful psychopomp or deity of death who seeks to ease the passing of a mortal of singular importance—such as a high-ranking priest of a death goddess. In such instances they serve as companions and ushers into the realm of the dead, not executioners. However, they’re capable of serving in both capacities, especially if misguided mortals try to keep them from their duty, using their deadly but painless kisses to end a life in an instant.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: psychopomp (+2 Str, +4 Dex, +4 Con, +2 Int, +2 Wis, +4 Cha) and NPC (­2 Int, +2 Cha).

Skills AthleticsB (2/+9), Bluff (4/+11), Concentration (9/+16), EnduranceB (2/+9), Fly (9/+15), Knowledge (lore) (5/+9), Knowledge (planes) (9/+13), KnowledgeB (warfare) (2/+6), Perception (9/+16), Planar Sense (9/+16), Stealth (9/+15)
Environment any (Purgatory)

Fear Aura (Sp) Spook (0 level) + Fell Frightening (+1 level) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) + Shape Spell (target to emanation; +2 levels) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Extend Spell (onset: inst. to 1 hr./level; +5 levels) + Reduce Spell (panicked to shaken; -1 level) = 4th level; those within 20 ft. are shaken 1 rd./level (Will 1 rd.).

Stern, silent, and cloaked in ragged black wings, vanth psychopomps serve as stoic guardians of Purgatory and watchers along the routes of the dead. Also known as reapers, angels of death, or amzranei, vanths protect the departed from those wishing to eat or steal their mortal souls, recapture escaped souls trying to flee their assigned fates, and are death’s foot soldiers against whatever would disrupt the natural cycle of mortality. They may also guard the dead and death’s assets, such as forgotten cemeteries, unattended mausoleums, and sacred groves.
Vanths are ancient creatures, perhaps predating the current gods of death, and are rumored to be ascended souls of a distant world of death-worshiping soldiers. They rarely speak or show emotion and their hollow voices carry unnaturally far. A vanth’s scythe is a badge of its station, reflecting its role as a harvester of souls. It features symbols in a language that was already lost when the death gods claimed Purgatory.
Most outsiders scorn vanths, as the psychopomps have no concern for law, rightfulness, or personal gain—only duty. Vanths view any outsider visiting Purgatory as a potential threat, and stalk angels and demons alike.

Psychopomp, Catrina

With lengthy curling hair, a dancer’s dress, and a bouquet of flowers, this woman remains beautiful, despite having no flesh. Catrinas always appear as festively dressed skeletons—usually in women’s garb but sometimes in colorful men’s formal wear, and usually decorated with or carrying f lowers. They do not have true genders, but an individual catrina may have a more masculine or feminine voice and personality. They typically stand between 5 and 6 feet tall and weigh about 20 to 30 pounds.

Compel Condemned (Sp) Compel (approach and kiss; 2nd level) + Extend Spell (1 rd. to 1 rd./level; +2 levels) + Pacific Spell (-2 levels) = 2nd level; as a standard action, a catrina can force one humanoid within Close range to approach and kiss her. This action is not considered to be against the target’s nature or self-destructive. Any damage taken by the target (other than damage the catrina deals) immediately ends this effect.

Kiss of Death (Sp) Ray of entropy (1st level) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) + Concentration Spell (standard; +2 levels) + Reduce Spell (10d6 to 5d6; -1 level) = 1st level; a catrina’s kiss deals 5d6 necrotic damage as a melee touch attack, and when continued counts as studying the victim for purposes of eventually using it to activate a Killing Stroke.

Catrinas welcome the dead into the afterlife, doing what they can to lessen the shock and terror experienced by mortals who haven’t accepted their own deaths or who still grieve for themselves. Eschewing the funereal themes and colors preferred by most other psychopomps, catrinas dress in festive shades, surrounding themselves with light and color to dispel a measure of death’s gloom. However, they don’t disguise their skeletal bodies, for despite any gilding they might put on the moment, they don’t seek to disguise the finality of death. A catrina’s motivation for easing the transition from life to death has more to do with making the soul’s progression calm than compassion for the soul—screaming and outrage disrupt the processing of the dead.

Catrinas rarely ever visit the Material Plane, but when they do so it’s typically at the command of a more powerful psychopomp or deity of death who seeks to ease the passing of a mortal of singular importance—such as a high-ranking priest of a death goddess. In such instances they serve as companions and ushers into the realm of the dead, not executioners. However, they’re capable of serving in both capacities, especially if misguided mortals try to keep them from their duty, using their deadly but painless kisses to end a life in an instant.

Stern, silent, and cloaked in ragged black wings, vanth psychopomps serve as stoic guardians of Purgatory and watchers along the routes of the dead. Also known as reapers, angels of death, or amzranei, vanths protect the departed from those wishing to eat or steal their mortal souls, recapture escaped souls trying to flee their assigned fates, and are death’s foot soldiers against whatever would disrupt the natural cycle of mortality. They may also guard the dead and death’s assets, such as forgotten cemeteries, unattended mausoleums, and sacred groves.

Vanths are ancient creatures, perhaps predating the current gods of death, and are rumored to be ascended souls of a distant world of death-worshiping soldiers. They rarely speak or show emotion and their hollow voices carry unnaturally far. A vanth’s scythe is a badge of its station, reflecting its role as a harvester of souls. It features symbols in a language that was already lost when the death gods claimed Purgatory.

Most outsiders scorn vanths, as the psychopomps have no concern for law, rightfulness, or personal gain—only duty. Vanths view any outsider visiting Purgatory as a potential threat, and stalk angels and demons alike.

sections.heading: Plant
sections.text:
The statistics for plant creatures are derived using the standardized racial rules (Chapter 2), with additional optional levels in the “plant creature” NPC class.
Type: Plants have the [plant] type. They breathe and eat (absorbing nutrients from the soil, from decaying matter, from prey, or from a combination of two or more of those). They do not sleep, but still need to rest to regain spells (in the case of Awakened plant spellcasters).
Languages: Plants do not gain any automatic languages.
Attribute Modifiers: +4 Str, +4 Con, -10 Int, –2 Cha: Plants are strong and hardy, but generally lack intelligence and personality (although they can gain both using the Awakened template). General plant monsters use the NPC stat array; those with levels in plant creature (see below) can use the elite array instead.
Racial Feats: Plants share the following:
Vegetable Constitution (Ex): Immune to paralysis, poison, polymorph, sleep effects, and stunning. Vegetative State (Ex): Immune to [mind-affecting] spells and effects that do not specifically target plants (although clerics with the Plant domain, verdant lord druids, and sorcerers with the Verdant bloodline all have ways of bypassing this immunity, as noted in Chapter 3).
Racial Traits:
Blind (Ex): Most plants are blind, and sense other creatures only through tremorsense (which they gain as do non-flying vermin). Sighted plant creatures have low-light vision instead.Energy Resistance (Ex): Plants also gain resistance 5 to one energy type (generally cold, fire, or electricity). A plant can gain vulnerability to one energy type in order to gain resistance to an additional type.Freeze (Ex): A plant creature can hold still, essentially Taking 20 on Stealth or Perform (acting); a successful opposed Perception check is needed to ascertain that the plant is animate. A character identifying the plant with a Profession (horticulturist) or Survival check is immediately aware of the plant’s true nature.
Weapon Familiarity: Plants are proficient with their natural weapons (usually two slam attacks), but gain no proficiency with manufactured weapons, armor, or shields.
Racial Progression: Plants generally advance through racial HD (+1 CR per 3 HD) or levels in the Plant Creature PC class (+1 CR per level).

Bonus Skills: Plant creatures receive 1 free rank per class level in Endurance; it is otherwise treated as a class skill.
Class Skills: Perception, Stealth.
Skill Points at Each Level: 2 + Int modifier.
Weapon and Armor Proficiency: None. However, plant creatures gain a bonus to natural armor that scales with level, as shown in the table.
Enhanced Resistance (Ex): At 1st level, the plant creature’s existing plant resistance(s) to energy increase(s) to 10.
Verdant Gift (Ex): At each class level, a plant creature gains a special ability. Typical examples are shown below, but other options of similar power can be substituted.

sections.heading: Assassin Vine
sections.text:
The assassin vine is a semi-mobile plant that collects its own grisly fertilizer by grabbing and crushing animals and depositing the carcasses near its roots. A mature plant consists of a main vine, about 20 feet long. Smaller vines up to 5 feet long branch off from the main vine about every 6 inches. These small vines bear clusters of leaves, and in late summer they produce bunches of small fruits that resemble wild grapes. The fruit is tough and has a hearty but bitter flavor. Assassin vine berries make a heady wine.

An assassin vine can move about, but usually stays put unless it needs to seek prey in a new vicinity. The plants use simple tactics, lying still until prey comes within reach and then attacking. Once an assassin vine is engaged, it pursues prey (albeit slowly) in order to catch and compost the creature. The plants prove tenacious, as long as their quarry remains within sight. Once a creature moves beyond the plant's ability to perceive it, the unthinking vine falls still and lies in wait for the next passerby.
Assassin vines lurk within dense forests and swamps, but some might encroach upon poorly tended fields and vineyards. The vine's seeds might be spread far by birds swift enough to pluck them and escape. Tales often tell of assassin vines appearing in flower beds or infiltrating greenhouses, murderous surprises planted by rivals and enemies or arbitrary doom dropped by unsuspecting wing.
A subterranean version of the assassin vine grows near hot springs, volcanic vents, and other sources of thermal energy. These plants have thin, wiry stems and gray leaves shot through with silver, brown, and white veins so that they resemble mineral deposits. An assassin vine growing underground usually generates enough offal to support a thriving colony of mushrooms and other fungi, which spring up around the plant and help conceal it.

A tendriculos is a creature brought into being through a corruption of nature, often where foul magic has seeped into the environs for many years, or where the boundaries between the Material Plane and the mysterious realm of the fey have worn thin. Tales and myths speak of arcane manipulation from other planes, while others speak of a tendriculos as being the manifestation of an angered spirit of nature.

A voracious carnivore, the tendriculos is an active hunter when it needs to be but it prefers to rely on ambush tactics, choosing well-traveled areas in the forest where it can lie in wait in the undergrowth. The creature is quick to swallow any prey it happens to catch in its vines, relying upon the acid-filled reservoir in its trunk to finish off prey that may still have a bit of fight left in it. This acid not only consumes organic material with shocking ease, but also contains a powerful paralytic enzyme that further reduces a creature's chance of escape once it's been gulped down by the plant.

html:
Plant

The statistics for plant creatures are derived using the standardized racial rules (Chapter 2), with additional optional levels in the “plant creature” NPC class.

Type: Plants have the [plant] type. They breathe and eat (absorbing nutrients from the soil, from decaying matter, from prey, or from a combination of two or more of those). They do not sleep, but still need to rest to regain spells (in the case of Awakened plant spellcasters).

Languages: Plants do not gain any automatic languages.

Attribute Modifiers: +4 Str, +4 Con, -10 Int, –2 Cha: Plants are strong and hardy, but generally lack intelligence and personality (although they can gain both using the Awakened template). General plant monsters use the NPC stat array; those with levels in plant creature (see below) can use the elite array instead.

Racial Feats: Plants share the following:

  • Vegetable Constitution (Ex): Immune to paralysis, poison, polymorph, sleep effects, and stunning.
  • Vegetative State (Ex): Immune to [mind-affecting] spells and effects that do not specifically target plants (although clerics with the Plant domain, verdant lord druids, and sorcerers with the Verdant bloodline all have ways of bypassing this immunity, as noted in Chapter 3).

Racial Traits:

  • Blind (Ex): Most plants are blind, and sense other creatures only through tremorsense (which they gain as do non-flying vermin). Sighted plant creatures have low-light vision instead.
  • Energy Resistance (Ex): Plants also gain resistance 5 to one energy type (generally cold, fire, or electricity). A plant can gain vulnerability to one energy type in order to gain resistance to an additional type.
  • Freeze (Ex): A plant creature can hold still, essentially Taking 20 on Stealth or Perform (acting); a successful opposed Perception check is needed to ascertain that the plant is animate. A character identifying the plant with a Profession (horticulturist) or Survival check is immediately aware of the plant’s true nature.

Weapon Familiarity: Plants are proficient with their natural weapons (usually two slam attacks), but gain no proficiency with manufactured weapons, armor, or shields.

Racial Progression: Plants generally advance through racial HD (+1 CR per 3 HD) or levels in the Plant Creature PC class (+1 CR per level).
