Bonus Skills: Plant creatures receive 1 free rank per class level in Endurance; it is otherwise treated as a class skill.

Class Skills: Perception, Stealth.

Skill Points at Each Level: 2 + Int modifier.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency: None. However, plant creatures gain a bonus to natural armor that scales with level, as shown in the table.

Enhanced Resistance (Ex): At 1st level, the plant creature’s existing plant resistance(s) to energy increase(s) to 10.

Verdant Gift (Ex): At each class level, a plant creature gains a special ability. Typical examples are shown below, but other options of similar power can be substituted.

  • Acid-loving plant: Immunity to acid.
  • Additional natural attack: Primary slam or other.
  • Blindsight: 30-ft. range.
  • Compressible: Damage reduction 10/slashing and immune to falling damage.
  • Constrict: The plant gains Improved Grapple and Vital Strike as bonus feats (if its BAB is +6 or higher).
  • Enhanced Attribute: Racial bonus of +1 per class level to one attribute score; stacks with existing racial bonuses.
  • Favored Terrain: With a +2 bonus, increasing to +4 at 4th level. The plant also gains pass without trace as a continuous spell-like ability. If the favored terrain is forests, the plant can gain speak with plants instead of speak with animals.
  • Grounded: The plant is immune to electricity.
  • Hydrophilic: Immunity to fire.
  • Magical Array (Sp). The plant gains a suite of racial spell-like abilities (Chapter 8).
  • Poisonous: Injury (one natural attack), inhaled (flowering plants or those with spore clouds), or contact (plants with noxious sap).
  • Regeneration: 2 hp/round per class level, negated by fire or bludgeoning damage.
  • Supernatural Ability (Su). This counts as two feats: either Magical Talent + Supernatural Ability, or else Permanent Spell + Feat Mastery.
  • Supple: Damage reduction 5/bludgeoning or slashing, and +4 to racial bonus to Dexterity.
  • Thick Bark (Ex): Class bonus to natural armor doubles.
  • Thorns (Ex): Non-reach melee attackers take 1d4 piercing damage per hit against the plant (for Medium plants; 1d6 for Large, etc.).

Assassin Vine

The assassin vine is a semi-mobile plant that collects its own grisly fertilizer by grabbing and crushing animals and depositing the carcasses near its roots. A mature plant consists of a main vine, about 20 feet long. Smaller vines up to 5 feet long branch off from the main vine about every 6 inches. These small vines bear clusters of leaves, and in late summer they produce bunches of small fruits that resemble wild grapes. The fruit is tough and has a hearty but bitter flavor. Assassin vine berries make a heady wine.

Giant plant creature 3

N Large plant [vine]

Init +0; Senses tremorsense 40 ft.; Perception +6

AC 15, touch 9, flat-footed 15 (-1 size, +6 natural)

hp 30 (3 HD; LW 15/HW 7)

Frequency uncommon

Organization solitary or patch (2-6)

An assassin vine can move about, but usually stays put unless it needs to seek prey in a new vicinity. The plants use simple tactics, lying still until prey comes within reach and then attacking. Once an assassin vine is engaged, it pursues prey (albeit slowly) in order to catch and compost the creature. The plants prove tenacious, as long as their quarry remains within sight. Once a creature moves beyond the plant's ability to perceive it, the unthinking vine falls still and lies in wait for the next passerby.

Assassin vines lurk within dense forests and swamps, but some might encroach upon poorly tended fields and vineyards. The vine's seeds might be spread far by birds swift enough to pluck them and escape. Tales often tell of assassin vines appearing in flower beds or infiltrating greenhouses, murderous surprises planted by rivals and enemies or arbitrary doom dropped by unsuspecting wing.

A subterranean version of the assassin vine grows near hot springs, volcanic vents, and other sources of thermal energy. These plants have thin, wiry stems and gray leaves shot through with silver, brown, and white veins so that they resemble mineral deposits. An assassin vine growing underground usually generates enough offal to support a thriving colony of mushrooms and other fungi, which spring up around the plant and help conceal it.

sections.heading: Blood Bush
sections.text:
The blood bush is a fell plant creature cursed in times past. It is named for its blood-red flowers and its thorny blood-red seeds. A blood bush is sometimes referred to as a “grave marker plant” because a creature that encounters it, and fails to see the danger this sinister plant presents, rarely lives to tell about it. The plant appears as a 3-foot tall flowering bush with a thick trunk and small whip-like branches. Each branch is topped with a blood-red flower and deep, rich green leaves.

Sonic Sensitivity (Ex) A blood bush that is subjected to a [sonic] effect loses its blindsight ability and is effectively blinded (loses its tremorsense) for 1d4+6 rounds.
A blood bush can only be grown from a seed that has germinated inside the warm body of a Small or larger animal. Roots from the germinating seed (represented as the poison effect) kill the host and use the nutrients provided to grow rapidly into a deadly plant. A number of nobles use this horrid plant as a deterrent against thieves and robbers, sometimes creating entire hedges of these plants. Blood bush seeds can be sold for about 20 gp each on the open market; collecting them and living to earn the money they bring is not the easiest of tasks.

When a blood bush detects a warm-blooded creature within 20 feet, it fires a volley of flower darts at the creature, attempting to implant it with its seeds. A normal blood bush has 30 flower darts total; these grow back at the rate of 1d6 per day. A creature that dies from the blood bush’s seed implantation rapidly decomposes, and a new blood bush springs up in the area within four days.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+2 Str, +0 Dex, +4 Con, +0 Int, +3 Wis, +0 Cha); verdant gifts: flower-darts, grounded, poison (implant seeds).

Wondrous nature of God only good,The beast hath root, the plant hath flesh and blood.The nimble plant can turn it to and fro,The nummed beast can neither stir nor goe,The plant is leafless, branchless, void of fruit,The beast is lustless, sexless, fireless, mute:The plant with plants his hungry paunch doth feede,Th’ admired beast is sowen a slender seed.

This massive ram-like creature's green pelt is actually a tangle of vines, and its horns are wickedly sharp wooden branches. A barometz, or “vegetable lamb of Tartary,” is a vegetable creature grown like fruit from a parent plant, and often cultivated by druids, who use them to help protect sacred groves.

html:
Barometz

But with true beasts, fast in the ground still sticking
Feeding on grass, and th’ airy moisture licking,
Such as those Borametz in Scythia bred
Of slender seeds, and with green fodder fed;
Although their bodies, noses, mouths, and eyes,
Of new-yeaned lambs have full the form and guise,
And should be very lambs, save that for foot
Within the ground they fix a living root
Which at their navel grows, and dies that day
That they have browzed the neighboring grass away.
Oh! Wondrous nature of God only good,
The beast hath root, the plant hath flesh and blood.
The nimble plant can turn it to and fro,
The nummed beast can neither stir nor goe,
The plant is leafless, branchless, void of fruit,
The beast is lustless, sexless, fireless, mute:
The plant with plants his hungry paunch doth feede,
Th’ admired beast is sowen a slender seed.

―Guillaume de Salluste du Bartas, La Semaine (1587)

sections.heading: Battlebriar
sections.text:
This six-legged lion-like creature has a body made of writhing vines and thorns. Each of its gorilla-like pairs of limbs is slightly shorter than the pair in front of it—its forelimbs are the longest, the middle pair of limbs slightly shorter, and its rear pair of legs the shortest of all. Long thorns protrude from every part of the creature’s body, making it seem impossible to approach or move around the creature without risking serious injury.
Plants magically engineered to serve as massive living siege engines, battlebriars on a field of battle can easily destroy massed formations of lesser troops. A lesser battlebriar averages around 8 feet long and weighs between 1 and 2 tons.
Battlebriar, LesserMM3	Cr 6
Giant plant creature 3
N Large plant
Init -1; Senses low-light vision; Perception +1
AC 17, touch 8, flat-footed 17
(-1 size, -1 Dex, +9 natural)
hp 126 (12 HD; LW 63/HW 31)
Immune plant traits
Resist electricity 10, fire 10
Fort +11, Ref +2, Int +6, Will +1
Weaknesses vulnerability to sonics
Spd 30 ft.
Melee 2 slams +14 (1d6+6/19-20 plus grab) or
2 Power Attacks +11 (1d6+12/19-20 plus grab)
Face 5 ft. x 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.;
threatened area is difficult terrain
Base Atk +9; CMB +16 (+20); CMD 26
Special Atks trample (2d6+9)
Supernatural Abilities (ML 12th)
2/day—thorn volley (see below; DC 22)
Attributes Str 23, Dex 8, Con 22, Int 5, Wis 12,    Cha 7
Feats Improved Critical, Impaling Attack, Improved Grapple, Improved Overrun, Power Attack, Vital Strike
Skills EnduranceB (3/+10), Stealth (12/+10)
Environment temperate forests
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary
Treasure none
Thorn Volley (Su) Invisible needle (0 level) + Cascade Spell (bind; +1 level) + Shape Spell (ray to burst; +2 levels) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 10’r.;  -1 level) = 2nd level, damage cap 5d6 piercing plus entangled in 10”r. (range 55 ft.).

Smaller than the more powerful battlebriars that roam the wild, “warbound impalers” are at least somewhat obedient and are often encountered in the service of another creature. Skilled handlers can influence these creatures enough to keep them docile much of the time, and even send them into battle when necessary.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+3 Str, +0 Dex, +2 Con, +4 Int, +2 Wis, -2 Cha); verdant gifts: improved natural armor, thorn field (as Thicket of Blades fighter talent), thorn volley. Although created for war, a few battlebriars have long since escaped the control of their creators, and they now roam through forest and field alike. Larger and more powerful than their domestic kin, a single greater battlebriar is capable of destroying a town, and for this reason it is an event of major importance when one is seen near a settlement of any size.
Battlebriar, GreaterMM2	Cr 13
Giant battlebriar
N Huge plant
Init -2; Senses low-light vision; Perception +16
AC 28, touch 11, flat-footed 23
(-2 size, -2 Dex, +5 dodge, +17 natural)
hp 324 (24 HD; LW 162/HW 81)
Immune plant traits
Resist electricity 10, fire 10
Fort +17, Ref +4, Int +9, Will +4
Weaknesses vulnerability to sonic
Spd 30 ft.
Melee slam +30/+25/+25/+25 (1d8+20/19-20/x3 plus grab) or Power Attack +25/+20/+20/+20 (1d8+35/19-20/x3 plus grab)
Face 10 ft. x 20 ft.; Reach 10 ft.;
threatened area is difficult terrain
Base Atk +18; CMB +30 (+36); CMD 38
Special Atks trample (6d6+15)
Supernatural Abilities (ML 24th)
10/day—greater thorn volley (see below; DC 31)
Attributes Str 30, Dex 6, Con 28, Int 5, Wis 12,    Cha 7
SQ freeze (DC 25)
Feats Dodge, Improved Critical, Impaling Attack, Improved Bull Rush, Improved Grapple, Improved Overrun, Permanent Spell (barkskin), Power Attack, Prana Practitioner, Vital Strike, Weapon Specialization
Skills EnduranceB (3/+15), Perception (12/+16), Stealth (12/+5)
Environment temperate forests
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary
Treasure none
Greater Thorn Volley (Su) Invisible needle (0 level) + Cascade Spell (bind; +1 level) + Augment Spell (grappled; +1 level) + Shape Spell (ray to burst; +2 levels) = 4th level, damage cap 15d6 piercing plus grappled 24 rds. in 20’r. (range 85 ft.).
